item.title: Bauchi governor signs law establishing Alkaleri Mining Institute
item.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi Bauchi State Governor, Senator Bala Mohammed, has signed into law a bill establishing the Mining Institute Alkaleri, Bauchi State (MIABAS), to promote mining education, develop technical skills and help tackle illegal mining. The development followed the passage of the bill by the Bauchi State House of Assembly, paving the way for the establishment of a specialised institution dedicated to mining education and technical skills development. A statement by the Information Officer of the Ministry of Natural Resources Development, Fatima AbdulKarim, said the governor had also approved the conversion of the Kaura Mineral Processing and Buying Centre at Gwaram village, Alkaleri Local Government Area, into the institute’s temporary site to facilitate its take-off. According to the statement, Mohammed also directed the relocation of the mineral processing and buying centre to Toro Local Government Area. AbdulKarim said the initiative was designed to develop local expertise, equip young people with industry-relevant skills and maximise the economic benefits of the state’s solid mineral resources. She said the institute would offer specialised training in mining, mineral processing, geology and related disciplines, creating opportunities for employment, entrepreneurship and greater local participation in the solid minerals value chain. The statement added that the establishment of MIABAS reflected the state government’s commitment to harnessing its mineral resources for sustainable economic growth and expanding opportunities for residents. Details of the institute’s administrative take-off, academic programmes and admission procedures, it said, would be announced through official channels. item.title: 2027: David Mark urges ECOWAS to warn FG, INEC against poll crisis
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Senator David Mark, has urged the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) to warn the Federal Government and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) against actions that could trigger a crisis over the 2027 general elections. Mark made the appeal in Abuja on Thursday when he received an ECOWAS delegation on a pre-election fact-finding mission, stressing that the credibility of Nigeria’s elections was critical to peace and stability across West Africa. According to a statement by the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the party said it had raised concerns over INEC’s preparedness, alleged government control of state institutions, including the judiciary, and threats of violence it attributed to the ruling party. Mark said credible elections were essential to preventing electoral conflict. “The best way to prevent conflict, especially in relation to elections, is to ensure that it is free, fair and transparent,” he was quoted as saying. He urged ECOWAS to join the ADC in pressing Nigerian authorities to ensure a credible electoral process. Mark said, “We in the ADC have committed ourselves to the highest standards of peaceful conducts before, during and after the elections. But we need ECOWAS to join us in insisting on a credible election now. “This is why you must tell the Federal Government and the INEC that they must not do anything that could plunge Nigeria into needless crisis. This must form a part of your early warning signals.” The Head of Mission and former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Mr Victor Bockarie Foh, said the delegation would report the ADC’s concerns, alongside those of other stakeholders, to the regional body. Foh said the mission was assessing Nigeria’s preparedness for the elections and the political atmosphere ahead of the polls, stressing that peace and stability in Nigeria were important to the entire West African region. Other members of the delegation included Francess Piage Alghali, ECOWAS Commissioner for Political Affairs, Peace and Security; Julius Fofanah Sandy, representing the ECOWAS Permanent Representatives’ Committee; and Segrine Mamadou, Head of the Electoral Assistance Division. item.title: Borno community to Tinubu, Zulum: Bring our 78 children home
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike & Kehinde Folarin ABUJA – The Margi community in Borno State has urged President Bola Tinubu and Governor Babagana Zulum to intensify efforts to rescue 78 schoolchildren and a teacher abducted from Mussa and Lassa communities in Askira/Uba Local Government Area. The community said the victims’ continued captivity had plunged their families into anguish, urging the authorities to step up rescue efforts and provide regular updates on their whereabouts. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Thursday, the community’s Secretary, Malla Gadzama, said 43 pupils were abducted from Mussa on May 15, 2026, while 35 students and a teacher were taken from a secondary school in Lassa on June 26 as they prepared for national examinations. “Our message is simple and clear: our children must not be forgotten,” Gadzama said. He called on Tinubu to mobilise the necessary security and intelligence resources and ensure effective coordination among security agencies. “Mr President, these children are Nigerians. Their lives matter,” he added. Gadzama also urged Zulum to make the rescue a priority and establish a reliable channel for keeping affected families informed without compromising security operations. “Development must also be measured by the safety of our children and the well-being of their families. Infrastructure cannot compensate for the continuing anguish of parents whose children remain in captivity,” he said. The community appealed to Senator Ali Ndume and other elected representatives from Askira/Uba to use their positions to sustain pressure on the authorities. It also called for better security around vulnerable schools and medical, psychological and educational support for the victims upon their return. Citing Section 14(2)(b) of the 1999 Constitution, which identifies the security and welfare of the people as the primary purpose of government, Gadzama said the authorities must fulfil their constitutional responsibility. “We are not asking for favour from government. We are just asking the government to fulfil its primary responsibility to the people,” he said. The community urged Tinubu, Zulum and security agencies to sustain rescue efforts until the children and their teacher were safely reunited with their families. “Bring Mussa schoolchildren, Lassa schoolchildren and their teachers safely home. That is our demand,” Gadzama said. The post Borno community to Tinubu, Zulum: Bring our 78 children home appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘No country developed in less than 30 years’, Kashifu defends Tinubu
item.description: .As TMS unveils new platform By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General of the National Information Technology Development Agency NITDA, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, has defended the reforms of President Bola Tinubu, saying no country has developed in less than 30 years. Kashifu, who is also Chairman, Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation (TMS), spoke on Thursday in Abuja at the group’s inaugural training workshop. “No country in the world developed in less than 30 years. The fastest developed country is South Korea. It took 30 years. To develop, you need the right policies first. That is the foundation Mr President is laying. Then you build on it to get investors,” he said. The programme, themed ‘Empowering Every Nigerian to be Heard’, also saw the Movement launch its official website, http://tmsnigeria.ng, where citizens can engage and verify information. The event was convened to educate citizens on the Renewed Hope Agenda and to give Nigerians a platform to contribute ideas on how to move the country forward. Kashifu said the thrust of the reforms is a change in what government spends its money on. “We spend most of our resources trying to subsidise consumption. When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu came on board, he looked at it: Is it consumption we should subsidise, or production, innovation, and investment? That is what the reforms are all about,” he said. According to him, the President built the Renewed Hope Agenda around eight priority areas. They are reforming the economy for sustained growth; strengthening national security; boosting agriculture for food security; unlocking energy and natural resources; enhancing infrastructure and transportation; focusing on health, education and social investment; accelerating diversification through industrialisation, digitalisation and creative industry; and improving governance through efficient service delivery. The NITDA chief pointed to the integration of digital skills into formal education, the introduction of Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) by the Ministry of Education, and the Student Loan scheme, which he said ensures no Nigerian is left behind because of economic circumstances. He added that NITDA is promoting digital literacy through Digital Literacy for All, the training of over 19,000 National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) champions in markets and motor parks, and the Three Million Tech Talent programme, which prepares young Nigerians to work remotely for global companies. Kashifu said the reforms are already attracting investors, citing the Dangote Refinery, a $1 billion data centre investment by a South African firm announced this week, and JP Morgan’s decision to open operations in Nigeria. “Reform is a journey; it is not a one-off event. The essence of this movement is to enlighten Nigerians on these reforms, so that Nigerians can understand what is in it for them. You are the ultimate beneficiary,” he said

item.title: ICPC arraigns PFIPC’s Adeyemi afresh on 22 counts
item.description: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) on Thursday arraigned Adeniyi Adeyemi afresh on 22 counts of alleged forgery, impersonation and related offences before an FCT High Court in Abuja over his purported role as director-general of the Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC). Adeyemi pleaded not guilty to all the counts. The fresh arraignment followed the striking out of an earlier eight-count charge against him by a Federal High Court in Abuja on October 12, after the Federal Government sought to terminate the proceedings following a review by the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF). Rotimi Oyedepo, Director of Public Prosecutions of the Federation, had told the court that the review established that the alleged offences fell within the jurisdiction of the FCT High Court rather than the Federal High Court, where the police initially filed the charge. The prosecution subsequently filed the fresh charge before the FCT High Court. Forgery, impersonation allegations In the new charge, the ICPC accused Adeyemi of forging a letter dated March 8, 2024, purportedly signed by Femi Gbajabiamila, Chief of Staff to the President, appointing him director-general of the PFIPC. The commission alleged that Adeyemi used forged documents to present the purported council as a legitimate government institution and gain access to government facilities and official processes. Other counts accuse him of forging an executive order purportedly establishing the council and a legislative instrument bearing the titles of the Presidential Economic Advisory Council and PFIPC. The ICPC also alleged that he forged a document addressed to the Accountant-General of the Federation seeking approval for the purported agency to operate within the government’s financial reporting structure. Another allegation concerns documents purportedly submitted to the National Information Technology Development Agency to obtain a domain name for the council. The commission further accused Adeyemi of using forged documents presented to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy to seek more than N27 billion for the establishment of the purported agency and N3.8 billion for personnel costs. In separate counts, the ICPC alleged that Adeyemi gave N210,000 to Aminu Abdullahi, an assistant chief technical officer in the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, to facilitate the allocation of office space without official authorisation. item.title: Ondo approves state burial for Fasoranti
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has set up a committee to organise a state burial for the late Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, who died at the age of 100. According to a statement issued in Akure by the governor’s Chief Press Secretary, Prince Ebenezer Adeniyan, the committee will work with the Fasoranti family and the leadership of Afenifere to organise a befitting burial for the elder statesman. The committee is chaired by the state Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Dr Kayode Ajulo, SAN, while Apostle Eniola Olushola will serve as secretary. Other members are Hon. Gbenga Fasua, Mr Gbenga Atiba, Mrs Kosemani Kolawole, Rt. Hon. Bakkita Bello, Hon. Idowu Otetubi, Erelu Modupe Martins, Mr George Asonja, Esq., Mr Muyiwa Ogunyemi, Hon. Stephen Abitogun and Mr Adetunji Gbenga. Adeniyan said the state government decided to honour Fasoranti with a state burial in recognition of his contributions to Ondo State, Yorubaland and Nigeria. He said Aiyedatiwa believed the late Afenifere leader deserved to be celebrated for his life of service, wisdom and selfless leadership. The governor also reaffirmed the government’s commitment to ensuring that the burial reflects Fasoranti’s contributions to society. The committee is expected to coordinate the arrangements in consultation with the family and Afenifere leadership to ensure a dignified farewell for the late nationalist. item.title: Ronaldo thanks fans after winning greatest Ballon d’Or award
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Cristiano Ronaldo has appreciated his fans and supporters around the world after his 2008 Ballon d’Or-winning season was voted the best in the history of the prestigious individual football award in a public poll organised to celebrate its 70th anniversary. The Ballon d’Or announced Ronaldo as the winner of its “Ballon d’Or of All Time” (BOAT) vote on Wednesday, after fans had their say in a poll that made them choose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season. In a post on X today, Ronaldo appreciated his fans, as he dedicated the award to them. He wrote: “Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours.” Football belongs to the fans! Thank you to all the fans around the world, the Ballon D’Or of All Time is also yours. pic.twitter.com/S0sLDNiUUY — Cristiano Ronaldo (@Cristiano) October 29, 2026 Ronaldo’s message followed his victory in the inaugural Ballon d’Or of All Time (BOAT) public vote, organised by France Football. Fans chose their favourite Ballon d’Or-winning season, and Ronaldo’s 2008 campaign finished ahead of Lionel Messi’s 2012 season. The 41-year-old winning season came with Manchester United in 2007–08, where he scored 42 goals in all competitions, including 31 in the Premier League and seven in the Champions League. United won both the Premier League and Champions League, with Ronaldo scoring in the final against Chelsea. His league tally earned him the European Golden Shoe, and he went on to win his first Ballon d’Or later that year. The Portuguese legend subsequently won the award four more times, in 2013, 2014, 2016 and 2017, taking his career tally to five. Lionel Messi’s 2012 season finished second in the poll, with Ronaldo’s 2017 campaign third. Messi’s 2023 season took fourth, while Ronaldo’s 2016 campaign rounded out the top five. The top ten also includes Ronaldo’s 2014 and 2013 seasons, plus Messi’s 2015, 2011 and 2009 campaigns. The BOAT vote was a fan poll celebrating the award’s 70th anniversary, rather than a new Ballon d’Or trophy. Voting opened on October 1 and closed on October 27, with the result announced on October 28. The post Ronaldo thanks fans after winning greatest Ballon d’Or award appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Makinde pledges to revive South-East industries
item.description: …Promises to tackle 25% interest rates, expand long-term financing By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU — The presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has pledged to tackle high interest rates and improve access to long-term financing to revive industries, expand businesses and create jobs in the South-East if elected president in 2027. Makinde, the Oyo State governor, made the pledge during a town hall meeting with stakeholders from the region in Enugu, where he identified manufacturing as a critical driver of economic growth, employment and poverty reduction. He said the South-East’s economic potential extended beyond trading to industrial production, particularly in commercial and manufacturing centres such as Onitsha and Nnewi in Anambra State. According to him, businesses cannot expand production or employ millions of Nigerians when interest rates remain high and long-term credit facilities are difficult to access. “Yes, trading is something this zone is synonymous with, but so is manufacturing. If you go to Onitsha and Nnewi, you will discover that the South-East is not just about trading; manufacturing is also thriving here. “You cannot expand manufacturing and employ millions of people when interest rates are at 25 per cent and long-term financing facilities are unavailable. These are two challenges we will tackle decisively,” he said. Makinde said his proposed economic reforms would shift Nigeria away from dependence on the sharing of federal allocations towards production, industrial expansion and wealth creation. “The responsibility of government is to create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive. That is precisely what we will do. We will create an enabling environment for businesses to flourish throughout the country,” he said. Drawing on his private-sector experience, the governor said access to long-term financing was essential for economic expansion, arguing that Nigeria’s financial system remained dominated by short-term loans largely suited to trading. “I come from the private sector. I started paying workers’ salaries at the age of 29, and now I am 58. I have been paying salaries from then until today, so I understand when an economy is expanding. “One indication of an expanding economy is the availability of long-term financing within the economic system. Right now, bankers can tell you that what we have been experiencing is mainly short-term financing facilities meant for trading,” he said. He said expanding manufacturing would help address unemployment, particularly among young people, and pledged to support entrepreneurs capable of creating sustainable jobs. Makinde cited the commissioning of the headquarters of Capital Sage, a conglomerate in Ibadan, as an example of the employment opportunities businesses could generate when given the right conditions to grow. item.title: 2027: Tinubu lacks energy to govern, Obi says
item.description: …Urges South-East to shun ethnic politics By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki ABAKALIKI — The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has questioned President Bola Tinubu’s competence and energy to govern Nigeria, urging him to leave office and rest. Obi spoke at an NDC town hall and stakeholders’ meeting held at the Citi-Hub Centre, Mile 50, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State, where he urged Nigerians to unite behind candidates based on their qualifications and capacity to deliver good governance rather than ethnic considerations. He cautioned the South-East against division, insisting that voters in Ebonyi and other parts of the country should support him based on his credentials, not because he is Igbo. “Let nobody divide the South-East. I don’t want the people of Ebonyi to vote for me because I am from the South-East. I don’t want you to vote for me because I am an Igbo person. “My dear people, I want you to vote for me because I am qualified to be the President of this country. I want you to vote for me because I am the leading candidate,” he said. The former Anambra State governor challenged Tinubu to explain his administration’s record over the past three years, particularly the use of funds borrowed by the Federal Government. “I want President Tinubu to come to Abakaliki to tell the people what he has done in the past three years. I want him to come to Abakaliki to tell you what he used the money he has been borrowing to do for the past three years,” Obi said. He also questioned the President’s reported time spent outside Nigeria, arguing that he should be able to travel across the country to account for his administration’s performance. “President Tinubu does not have the competence to run Nigeria. He does not have the energy to run Nigeria. He should pack his things, go home and rest,” Obi said. Outlining his proposed priorities if elected president in 2027, Obi said his administration would declare emergencies in key sectors, including national unity, security, education, healthcare, corruption and food production. On national unity, he said his government would seek to reduce ethnic divisions and ensure that appointments reflected the federal character principle. “We must unite this country. Our pride should not be consideration of employment, this or that. We will operate federal character for all the jobs we have. So, we must unite the country,” he said. On security, Obi promised decisive action against insecurity and pledged to equip security agencies to protect lives and property. “We will declare emergency in the security of lives and property in Nigeria. We will deal with insecurity decisively. Nobody will be in charge, we will be in charge,” he said. item.title: 154 students hospitalised over suspected drug reaction in Katsina
item.description: One hundred and fifty-four students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, Katsina State, were hospitalised following a suspected adverse reaction to praziquantel tablets administered to treat bilharzia. The incident occurred on Monday, according to a statement issued on Wednesday by the Katsina State Police Command’s Public Relations Officer, Abubakar Sadiq Aliyu. Aliyu said the students reportedly developed symptoms of an adverse drug reaction after receiving the tablets from the school authorities. Praziquantel is used to treat schistosomiasis, also known as bilharzia, a parasitic disease associated with contact with freshwater contaminated by the parasites. The police spokesman said the affected students were taken to hospital for treatment, with no casualties or deaths recorded. He added that the remaining 25 students, who had been kept in hospital for further medical attention, had also been treated and discharged. According to him, all the affected students were in good health and had been reunited with their families and schoolmates. The Commissioner of Police, Ali Umar Fage, thanked members of the public for their cooperation and calmness during the incident. He urged residents to refrain from spreading unverified reports and rumours, assuring them that the command would continue to protect lives and property across the state. item.title: INEC moves to tackle electoral risks in Abia
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has stepped up preparations for the 2027 general elections, with efforts to identify and address potential threats to peaceful and credible polls in Abia State. The Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in the state, Prof. Sylvia Agu, disclosed this on Thursday in Umuahia at a stakeholder sensitisation workshop on Electoral Risk Management (ERM). Agu said early identification of electoral threats, effective coordination and collaboration among stakeholders were critical to preventing disruptions and strengthening public confidence in the electoral process. “Successful elections require deliberate preparation, effective coordination and the collective commitment of all institutions and individuals involved in the electoral process,” she said. She urged stakeholders, particularly security agencies, to sustain their cooperation with INEC to ensure peaceful elections and strengthen democracy. The Abia State Commissioner of Police, CP Wilfred Olutokunbo Afolabi, also reaffirmed the police commitment to credible elections. Represented by the Deputy Commissioner of Police in charge of Operations, DCP Ifeanyi Uzor, Afolabi said the police would protect election materials, provide security for National Youth Service Corps members and ensure a safe environment for voters. “The 2027 election will not be an exception. We have a renewed commitment from the Inspector-General of Police to ensure credible elections in 2027. That duty we must perform without fear or prejudice,” he said. Also speaking, the INEC Administrative Secretary in Abia, Chief Ama Agwu, said the ERM framework would help identify, assess and manage security threats, political tensions, environmental challenges and operational difficulties capable of disrupting elections. Agwu urged electoral officers to ensure that information gathered was accurate, verified and reflective of conditions on the ground to facilitate timely interventions. Earlier, the Head of the Department of Planning and Monitoring, Mr Ogbuisi Robinson, said the workshop was designed to identify electoral risks specific to Abia, strengthen early-warning and response mechanisms, and promote evidence-based planning. He said the exercise would also involve collaboration with the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES). INEC officials, including Electoral Officers from all 17 local government areas in Abia, representatives of security agencies and other stakeholders attended the workshop. item.title: ICPC docks alleged ‘fake’ PFIPC DG Adeyemi for forgery, impersonation
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) on Thursday arraigned the self-styled Director-General (DG) of the alleged “non-existent” Presidential Foreign Investment Promotion Council (PFIPC), Prince Adeniyi Adeyemi, on a 22-count charge relating to forgery and impersonation. Adeyemi, who has been in detention since July 14, was docked before Justice Halilu Yusuf of the High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting in Maitama. The ICPC alleged that the defendant, while passing himself off as a public servant, obtained over N27 billion to start the fake agency. He was also alleged to have dubiously obtained another N3.8 billion for personnel costs. The prosecution told the court that Adeyemi also obtained funds through a forged document addressed to the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy. It alleged that the defendant forged documents purportedly signed by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila, which he claimed appointed him Director-General of PFIPC, and used them to occupy government office facilities at the Federal Secretariat Complex Phase III, Abuja. Besides, Adeyemi was accused of forging a document addressed to the Accountant-General of the Federation, captioned “RE: REQUEST FOR APPROVAL OF SELF-ACCOUNTING STATUS”, for the non-existent agency to operate within the government financial reporting structure. He was said to have forwarded forged documents to the DG of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) to get a domain name for the agency. The defendant was also accused of gifting N210,000, without official authorisation, to one Aminu Abdullahi, an Assistant Chief Technical Officer in the Office of the Secretary General of the Federation (OSGF), “to facilitate the allocation of office space.” He allegedly gifted another N300,000 to Ogaba Harry, an officer in the Office of the Chief Economic Adviser to the President, to facilitate the release and handover of two official vehicles, a Prado SUV and a Land Cruiser SUV, to him. Other counts in the charge included an allegation that on July 29, 2025, the defendant collected N20 million from one Oyekunle Gbenga, the Managing Director of Divine Dopacy Nigeria Limited, under the false pretence of a “project facilitation loan” for a purported N2.8 billion contract allegedly awarded by the fictitious agency for the procurement of furniture and renovation of the official residence of the DG of the said non-existent PFIPC. The ICPC insisted that he committed the offences between 2024 and 2026. He was said to have contravened Sections 364, 366 and 132 of the Penal Code Cap. 532, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (Abuja) 1990; Section 1(1)(a) of the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Fraud Related Offences Act, 2006, punishable under Section 1(3); and Section 9(a) of the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act, 2000, punishable under Section 9(b). item.title: ‘Horrific’ Russian Drone Strike Kills 14 At Ukraine Train Station
item.description: A Russian drone slammed into a busy platform at a railway station in Ukraine’s Dnipro on Thursday killing at least 14 people in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called a “horrific” attack that demands a response from Kyiv’s allies. The strike came as Ukraine and Russia strive to uphold a fragile local ceasefire in the ravaged city of Oleshky — under Russian occupation since 2022 and where residents have faced months of food, water and medicine shortages. The truce was holding into its third day, both countries said, with the Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets announcing that he had “set out with the Ukrainian delegation towards Oleshky” through Belarus and Russia. But elsewhere, Moscow continued to pummel Ukraine. The strike at the Dnipro train station hit a platform “where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing”, Zelensky said. By early Thursday afternoon, Dnipropetrovsk regional governor Oleksandr Ganzha said the death toll from the strike had risen to 14. EDITORS NOTE: Graphic content / In this handout photograph taken and released by the Ukrainian Emergency Service on October 29, 2026, Ukrainian law enforcement officers work at the site of an air attack on the railway station in Dnipro, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo by Handout / UKRAINIAN EMERGENCY SERVICE / AFP) Another 14 had been wounded, he said, adding that six of them were in severe condition after suffering “multiple shrapnel wounds”, including an 11-year-old boy and a man who had “both legs amputated”. Zelensky slammed the attack as “horrific” and insisted that “sanctions against Moscow and its war machine must not be eased for as long as this Russian war continues”. Images released by Ukrainian emergency services showed bodies on the platform, rescuers helping victims to safety and two burnt-out passenger trains with their windows shattered. French President Emmanuel Macron reacted with outrage to the attack, stressing the need for “far more than a localised ceasefire” like the one in Oleshky. “It is intolerable that Russia continues to reject all proposals to this end, choosing instead to pursue escalation and target civilians,” he said on X. Zelensky slams sanctions relief Russia has fired drones on trains across Ukraine since the first days of its 2022 invasion — destroying hundreds of locomotives and killing several railway workers. Ukraine’s air force said it had intercepted three jet-powered drones in a daytime attack, but that a fourth evaded its defences and hit the station. In the aftermath of the attack, Zelensky refreshed his criticism of a deal struck this month between US President Donald Trump and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin to ease some sanctions on Russia allowing Moscow to release diesel onto global markets. “How many such terrorist strikes has Russia carried out against our people since sanctions were lifted on some Russian oligarchs and the energy sector, instead of de-escalating,” he asked. At
